chunk-001:c004.proposition: The argument requires only the existence of some necessary truth rather than conceivability as a test or the necessity of any particular law of logic.

orphanFallback.rationale: Independently of the objection it answers, this states the argument's minimal modal starting premise and limits the commitment required of the pro route.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Propositions are best understood as thoughts because their intrinsic intentionality is explained by mentality, a familiar ontological category already instantiated by thoughts.

orphanFallback.rationale: The move directly supplies the route's central positive inference from propositional aboutness and aspectual shape to a mental ontology.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Divine conceptualism explains both propositional intentionality and causal relevance better than a Platonist realm of causally inert abstract objects, so parsimony is not the sole comparative consideration.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a standalone comparative argument, it identifies intentionality and causal relevance as affirmative explanatory advantages of divine conceptualism over Platonism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: The distinction between a human thought and its shareable propositional content need not apply to God, because divine thoughts can themselves constitute the contents shared by human thoughts.

orphanFallback.rationale: This positively specifies how divine cognition grounds objective, shareable content: divine thoughts serve as contents rather than containing further propositions.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: Although divine and human cognition differ, both remain genuinely intentional because each consists in cognitive direction toward things under particular aspects.

orphanFallback.rationale: The shared features of directedness and aspectual shape independently establish the continuity needed to classify divine cognitive acts as genuine thoughts.

chunk-003:c003-01.proposition: Divine conceptualism combines the Platonist requirements of objectivity and necessary existence with the conceptualist requirement that propositions possess intrinsic mentality.

orphanFallback.rationale: The comparison independently presents divine conceptualism as satisfying the central explanatory demands motivating both realism and conceptualism.

chunk-003:c003-03.proposition: Explaining a thought's intentionality by appeal to prior propositional content presupposes the disputed non-theistic Platonist framework and is therefore question-begging in this dispute.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a constructive burden-setting distinction, it shows why an appeal to independent content cannot itself explain intentionality without first defending Platonism.

chunk-003:c003-07.proposition: Ordinary-language commitments and explanatory needs involving undiscovered truths, shared beliefs, communication, and translation jointly support realism about propositions.

orphanFallback.rationale: The candidate is already a standalone constructive case, grounding proposition realism in several source-identified linguistic and explanatory phenomena.
